minutes.headline: Water commissioners added a 1.5-inch connection fee and will interview new attorneys before June 30.
minutes.summary: The Water District commissioners reviewed new legal counsel proposals and planned interviews of three firms, hoping to keep the outgoing attorney on as a consultant past June 30. They voted to add a connection fee for 1.5-inch services, prompted by a request for a separate line to fill a hydroseeder. The superintendent also reported a staff departure, a possible 40B development and PFAS results.

public_comment.topic: Asked where the district stands on PFAS and suggested publicizing test results for public relations.
Advised the district to hire a firm larger than a sole operator, preferably local, with contract, DEP and municipal law skills; cautioned about costs if a court case arises.
Commented on the employment and hiring difficulty, concerned only with the Lunenburg Water District.

votes.motion: Add a connection fee for a 1.5-inch service to the rules and regulations at the amount heard as 9 500.

budget_items.what_was_said: One attorney quoted an hourly rate with a lower rate for an associate and nothing for administrative staff. A larger firm quoted a lower hourly rate; no retainer.
Typical annual legal use was estimated as modest hours.
Existing fees were discussed for one-inch and two-inch connections, with no 1.5-inch fee.
Fee set at the midpoint between the one-inch and two-inch fees.
Commissioners agreed to check pay against other employers since the water industry is competitive.

decisions.decision: Superintendent to schedule interviews with three law firms at one of the upcoming meetings.
Board favored asking the outgoing attorney to stay as a consultant past June 30.
Superintendent to start drafting a job ad for the licensed operator position.
Superintendent to call around for a salary survey.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted to add a connection fee for a 1.5-inch service to the district's rules and regulations; the amount is as heard in the captions.
The fee sits between the existing one-inch and two-inch fees and was prompted by a request from a grounds company for a separate line to fill a hydroseeder.
The board favored asking the outgoing attorney to stay on as a consultant past June 30, and the superintendent will schedule interviews with three law firms.
The superintendent will start drafting a job ad for the licensed operator position and call around for a salary survey after reporting a staff departure.
The superintendent also raised a possible 40B development, and a resident asked where the district stands on PFAS.

why_it_matters: The new fee sets what a customer pays to connect a 1.5-inch service, a size the rules did not price before, so it touches anyone building or upgrading a connection.
A change of legal counsel and a vacant licensed operator post bear on how the district handles contracts, DEP matters and on-call water coverage, and on the pay it may need to offer.
watch_next: Interviews of three law firms at an upcoming commissioners' meeting, before the June 30 end of the outgoing attorney's term.
The salary survey and the licensed operator job ad the superintendent is to prepare.
